easy.def: To make strong.
examples: Walls fortify the castle.
Food will fortify you.
They fortified the fort.

more.def: To make something stronger, especially against an attack.
examples: The builders fortified the castle walls with stone.
Cereal is fortified with extra vitamins.
A good breakfast will fortify you for the day.

easy.def: Two weeks.
examples: We will stay a fortnight.
A fortnight is two weeks.
The trip lasted a fortnight.

more.def: A period of two weeks.
examples: We are going on vacation for a fortnight.
The library lets you keep a book for a fortnight.
A fortnight is fourteen days.

easy.def: A strong building or place that is built to keep people safe from attack.
examples: The fortress had thick walls.
We visited a fortress.
The fortress is made of stone.

more.def: A strong place with thick walls that is built to protect people from attack.
examples: The fortress had thick stone walls and tall towers.
We visited an old fortress on a hill.
Soldiers once guarded the fortress day and night.

easy.def: Lucky.
examples: We were fortunate to have sun.
She is fortunate.
He was fortunate to win.

more.def: Having good luck.
examples: We were fortunate that the rain held off.
She is fortunate to have so many friends.
He was fortunate to find his lost key.

easy.def: By good luck.
examples: Fortunately, it did not rain.
Fortunately, no one was hurt.
Fortunately, I had a map.

more.def: By good luck, in a way that turns out well.
examples: Fortunately, the doctor was nearby.
Fortunately, no one was hurt in the fall.
Fortunately, I had packed an extra coat.

easy.def: A lot of money.
examples: He made a fortune.
The family has a fortune.
The pirate hid a fortune.

more.def: A very large amount of money.
examples: The pirate hid his fortune on the island.
She made a fortune selling lemonade.
The family inherited a fortune.

easy.def: Luck.
examples: Good fortune.
Fortune smiled on us.
Bad fortune.

more.def: Luck, good or bad, that comes to a person.
examples: We had good fortune on our trip.
Fortune smiled on the team.
Bad fortune kept the ship in port.

easy.def: The number 40.
examples: I have forty stickers.
Forty kids came.
There are forty chairs.

more.def: The number that comes after thirty-nine, written 40.
examples: There are forty students in the gym.
He counted to forty by fours.
The trip took forty minutes.

easy.def: Toward the front.
examples: Step forward.
Move forward.
The car rolled forward.

more.def: In the direction that is in front of you.
examples: Please step forward and take a ticket.
The line moved forward.
He leaned forward to hear better.

easy.def: In the direction in front of you.
examples: Move forwards, please.
He leaned forwards.
The line moved forwards.

more.def: Toward the front, or in the direction you are facing.
examples: The line slowly moved forwards.
She leaned forwards to hear the story.
The car rolled forwards down the small hill.

easy.def: A very old bone or mark from a plant or animal, found in rock.
examples: We saw a dinosaur fossil.
I found a fossil of a shell.
The fossil is in a rock.

more.def: What is left of a plant or animal from long ago, kept safe in rock.
examples: The fossil showed the shape of a fish that lived millions of years ago.
Fossils help scientists learn about animals from long ago.
He found a leaf fossil in a piece of stone.

easy.def: Very dirty or bad-smelling.
examples: The foul smell was strong.
The water was foul.
The foul weather kept us in.

more.def: Very dirty, bad-smelling or unpleasant.
examples: A foul smell came from the old trash can.
The foul weather kept us indoors.
The water in the pond was foul.

easy.def: A move in a game that breaks the rules.
examples: The player made a foul.
The referee called a foul.
That was a foul.

more.def: An unfair move that breaks the rules of a sport.
examples: The referee blew the whistle for a foul.
He got a foul for pushing.
The team lost a point on the foul.

easy.def: The solid base that a building stands on.
examples: The house has a strong foundation.
The foundation is made of stone.
Workers poured the foundation.

more.def: The strong base under a building, which holds it up.
examples: The house has a strong foundation of stone.
Workers poured the concrete foundation first.
A good foundation keeps the walls from cracking.

easy.def: A person who starts a school, a club or a town.
examples: The founder of our school was kind.
She is the founder of the club.
A statue of the founder stands here.

more.def: A person who starts something new, such as a town, a school or a business.
examples: The founder of our town built the first house beside the river.
A statue of the school's founder stands near the front gate.
The founder of the company started by selling lemonade on the street.

easy.def: To fill with water and sink.
examples: The old boat foundered.
The ship foundered in the storm.
The raft foundered near the rocks.

more.def: To fill with water and sink, or to fail completely.
examples: The little boat foundered on the rocks and began to fill with water.
The plan foundered when the money ran out.
The ship foundered in the big storm and sank to the bottom.

easy.def: Water that shoots up in the air.
examples: The fountain is in the park.
We tossed a penny in the fountain.
The fountain sprays water.

more.def: A stream of water that shoots up into the air, or a structure that makes it.
examples: We tossed a penny into the fountain.
The fountain in the square sparkled in the sun.
Kids splashed in the park fountain.

easy.def: The number 4.
examples: I have four crayons.
Four plus one is five.
A cat has four legs.

more.def: The number 4, which is one more than three.
examples: A year has four seasons.
We saw four deer by the road.
The clock struck four.

easy.def: One more than thirteen.
examples: She has fourteen pencils.
My brother is fourteen.
Fourteen ducks swam by.

more.def: The number 14, which comes after thirteen and before fifteen.
examples: Two weeks is fourteen days.
The bus has fourteen rows of seats.
He read fourteen books this summer.

easy.def: Number four in a line.
examples: I am in fourth place.
Fourth grade is fun.
The fourth day was sunny.

more.def: Coming after the third one and before the fifth one.
examples: She finished fourth in the race.
The fourth chapter is my favorite.
My brother is in fourth grade this year.

easy.def: One of four equal parts.
examples: I ate a fourth of the pie.
A fourth is the same as a quarter.
She gave me a fourth of the sandwich.

more.def: One of four equal parts that make a whole.
examples: Cut the cake into fourths so each of us gets a piece.
A fourth of the class walks to school.
Add a fourth of a cup of sugar.

easy.def: A bird kept for food or eggs, like a chicken.
examples: The fowl pecked at the seed.
A fowl is a bird.
Chickens and ducks are fowl.

more.def: A bird such as a chicken, duck or turkey that is raised for eggs or meat.
examples: The farmer fed the fowl in the morning.
Chickens and ducks are kinds of fowl.
The fowl pecked at the grain.
